reviews_5s:
I plan to use this for my sourdough between bakes. It is a good size for the first build-up to 250 grams at 8-12 hours before I start my dough. Other sizes available for many purposes. Easy to clean thanks to the straight edges- screw capped canning jars are difficult when dried culture gets in the threads. Well made, but I can see myself breaking the metal clips that hold the lid on top. Won't matter for my purpose, really, since I don't want it tightly sealed, anyway. Very cute if you want them visible on a shelf, full of beans or whatever. I definitely recommend.Weck is top quality! I am a newcomer in
sourdough colonies, am baking smaller
loaves in an air fryer about every 2 weeks.
I tried larger cups & bowls that are better
suited for people who bake more often
for more people. What a mess when
feeding the colony and transferring
the leftover dough to discard!
The half liter size is perfect for a
small colony of 50 to 100 grams.
The 1/4 L size is ideal for discard.
It’s easy to label those and stack
them in the fridge to make waffles,
pancakes, etc. Feeding and cleaning
up are much easier than a large
measuring cup or bowl.
Worth every penny!SO CUTE AND USEFUL!

This jar has so many different uses!! I have been loving it recently to make coffee and fun drinks. I love it so much because it is the best size and super light weight. I got two for the amount that I purchased and I couldn’t recommend this enough! Amazing quality! Run & get yours!Excellent quality jars that I will be able to use in endless ways! Even iced coffee drinks as of recent.I love it so muchh that I ordered more of it. Got in different sizes too. The quality is really good even the small cup lid that I have, I accidentally dropped it and it's still good. Could feel the weight but still comfortable to use. Pretty good for the priceLove these for drinking glasses wish they were not so expensive I would buy more.So good ! Perfect size no leaks and nice thick glass was worried it was super overpriced but they are worth itIf you do sourdough, just get them now!! I used mason jars to mix my starter for over a year, because I already had them so why buy something else. Trust me, BUY THEM NOW! The straight sides are so easy to scrape and clean. It’s easy to tell how much it’s risen/doubled. The glass lid…no fighting rust spots…without the seal keeps it covered while letting gasses escape, or with the seal makes it airtight for storing in the fridge. I got this smaller size mostly for storing my starter in the fridge when not using, & maintaining a small daily feed on days I’m not baking. I also bought the larger size for when I’m making larger amounts for bake days. They are great quality, fairly thick glass so durable as long as you don’t drop it from the microwave on the tile floor (ask me how I know :/ ), and simply make life easier!I don't use this jars for canning so I can't speak to the quality but I really like these for making drinks. Once the lid is properly secure the jars are leak proof (to an extent) I feel like the clips are not very secure and pop off easy but for me, it is not a huge deal.These are great little jars. They both fit in the Instant Pot to make yogurt. I think there is a sacrifice of screw on lids or snap tight, for the clip on glass lid. Just depends upon your need. These are easy to use, heavyweight, a little pricey, but hold a good amount with a wide mouth.
